profile.stagger_pattern: Five at-large Township Committee seats on 3-year staggered terms in a repeating 1-2-2 pattern: 1 seat elected Nov 2018/2021/2024 (terms 2019-21, 2022-24, 2025-27); 2 seats elected Nov 2016/2019/2022/2025 (terms 2017-19, 2020-22, 2023-25, 2026-28); 2 seats elected Nov 2017/2020/2023 (terms 2018-20, 2021-23, 2024-26). Terms begin January 1.
profile.notes: Franklin Township, GLOUCESTER County (Franklinville, NJ 08322) - confirmed, not Somerset/Hunterdon/Warren. Traditional NJ Township Committee form: the committee selects the Mayor (Chairman) and Deputy Mayor (Vice Chairman) from among its own members annually at the January 1 reorganization meeting; neither office ever appears on a ballot. Elections are partisan, at the November general. Official website is franklintownshipnj.org (franklintownship.com is a meta-refresh redirect to it).

run_log.detail: IDENTITY CONFIRMED, three ways. (1) NJ DCA Mayors JSON API (data.nj.gov/resource/gkt3-i954.json?$q=Franklin) returned four NJ Franklin Townships; only the Gloucester one (dlgs 805, Franklinville 08322) has mayor John Bruno, with a term ending 2026-12-31 - a one-year term, consistent with annual committee selection. (2) Township resolution R-16-2024 reads 'Township Committee of the Township of Franklin, County of Gloucester'. (3) Gloucester County Clarity carries the contest 'TOWNSHIP COMMITTEE - TOWNSHIP OF FRANKLIN' with Doyle and Fiorella - the same people in the minutes. No evidence pointed to Somerset, Hunterdon or Warren. Note franklin-twp.org is the HUNTERDON township and is a search decoy.

CENSUS VERDICT OVERTURNED. The census listed this township as having NO WORKING ARCHIVE (CivicEngage/Granicus, robots-blocked). Wrong on both counts. The recorded domain franklintownship.com is only a 108-byte meta-refresh to the real site, www.franklintownshipnj.org - testing the redirect target rather than the recorded domain is what unlocked the city. That host returns 200 to plain curl with a browser UA, and its robots.txt disallows only /admin, /search.aspx and similar - the archive paths are explicitly permitted. It is CivicPlus (older .aspx generation) with a full AgendaCenter and DocumentCenter. This makes 5 of the 8 'no archive' cities now overturned.

Five at-large seats, 3-year staggered terms, 1-2-2 pattern, partisan November general, terms starting January 1. Derived from the eight reorganization records, which each announce the preceding general election and the number of seats filled; the pattern closes consistently across all eight years with no leftover or missing seat.

AgendaCenter category id for Township Committee is 3 (found via the 'category-panel-N' aria-controls attributes; the CID= values exposed on the page, 15 and 16, are document categories and are the wrong ones). The dated search endpoint /AgendaCenter/Search/?term=&CIDs=3&startDate=&endDate= returns ONLY the current year regardless of the range given, so it could not reach 2019-2025. Fell back to sweeping the ViewFile integer id space (the date segment is confirmed cosmetic - every document fetched correctly with a constant _01012020- prefix). Swept ids 200-1210, 860 documents retrieved, then indexed by first-page text. This yielded 168 Township Committee minutes covering 2019-2026 continuously.

TENANT-CONTAMINATION CHECK PASSED. Per the skill's warning that CivicPlus integer id spaces are shared across tenants, every swept document was checked for the city name in its extracted text; all 860 were Franklin Township (Gloucester) bodies. The id space DOES interleave bodies within the tenant - id 626, adjacent to the 2021 reorganization, is a Unity Advisory Committee meeting, and the lower range is non-chronological (2013 minutes sit at ids 263-279, 2018 at 234-237). Body was confirmed per document, not assumed from id proximity.

THREE DATE DEFECTS CAUGHT IN THE SOURCE DOCUMENTS, all by day-of-week/impossibility checking. (1) The 2022 reorganization minutes carry the header 'January 1, 2021' but announce the November 2, 2021 election and elect a mayor 'for the year 2022' - it is the 2022 reorganization, and id ordering confirms it (it sits between the 2022-01-25 and 2022-02-08 minutes). Taking the header at face value would have produced two conflicting 2021 reorganizations and lost 2022 entirely. (2) The 2020-01-01 minutes report 'the November 5, 2020 General Election' - impossible for a meeting held ten months earlier; Nov 5 2019 was a Tuesday, Nov 5 2020 a Thursday. (3) The 2025-01-01 minutes report 'the November 5, 2025 General Election' - same defect; the real cycle is 2024-11-05. All election dates recorded here were day-of-week checked against a Tuesday.

MANDATORY CHECK RUN, and it found the only mid-term change in the panel. Rather than searching, the roll call was extracted from all 168 Township Committee minutes and diffed year over year. That surfaced Timothy Doyle appearing on 2020-02-11 - eleven months before the election that the reorganization minutes credit him to. Tracing it back: Leah Vassallo's resignation was accepted at the 2019-12-30 meeting; the 2020-01-01 reorganization and the 2020-01-14 work session list only FOUR members; and the 2020-01-14 regular meeting carries 'Motion R-28-20 Appointing Timothy Doyle To Fill the Vacant Position on the Franklin Township [Committee]', with Doyle sworn in that evening. He then won the seat outright in November 2020. Reading the election record alone would have shown Doyle starting 2021-01-01 and left 2020 with a phantom fifth member.

CAVEAT, NOT A GAP (filed here per the brief rather than in gaps). Committee Seat E was lawfully vacant 2020-01-01 to 2020-01-13, thirteen days between Vassallo's resignation taking effect and Doyle's appointment. The 2020 seat-year is sourced by Doyle for the remaining 353 days, so this is a soft boundary date on a sourced cell, not an uncovered one. No other vacancy, resignation, death or recall occurred in 2019-2026: the roll-call diff shows composition changing only at January 1 boundaries in every other year.

One cycle needed escalation. The 2024-01-01 reorganization minutes are genuinely ABSENT from the AgendaCenter Minutes archive (ids 968-981 in that window are other bodies; kinds Minutes, Agenda and ArchivedMinutes were all tried), leaving the 2023 cycle and the 2024 mayoralty unsourced. Two independent routes closed it. (a) The CivicPlus site search /Search/Results?searchPhrase= returns extracted PDF TEXT plus the DocumentCenter id - it surfaced Resolution R-16-2024 at /DocumentCenter/View/6192, which names both the 2024 Mayor and Deputy Mayor verbatim. This confirms the skill's note that the site search is worth more than the archive when the archive has a hole. (b) Gloucester County Clarity supplied the 2023-11-07 municipal contest itself.

REGISTRY CORRECTION CONFIRMED AND EXTENDED - Clarity is NOT robots-blocked. results.enr.clarityelections.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404, so no Disallow exists. The Gloucester County JSON API is fully open to plain curl and CARRIES MUNICIPAL CONTESTS, which the NJ state PDFs do not. Working recipe: the county's own Previous Election Results page at gloucestercountynj.gov/1252 lists every Clarity election id as a plain link (25 of them, 2011-2026); then /NJ/Gloucester/{id}/current_ver.txt gives the version and /NJ/Gloucester/{id}/{ver}/json/en/summary.json gives the full contest array. Nov 2023 general = id 118787, ver 324803. Its contest 'TOWNSHIP COMMITTEE - TOWNSHIP OF FRANKLIN' returned MARK J. FIORELLA 2647, TIMOTHY DOYLE 2532, MARIO CHRISTINA 1776, NO NOMINATION MADE 0, WRITE-IN 89. Note electionsettings.json did not expose a title/date under the keys tried - identify the election from its contest list instead (the 2023 one carries STATE SENATE - 3RD LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT). No Gloucester County canvass PDF was needed, and none was found in the Camden path form.

VERBATIM CHECK. Every name in this file comes from locally extracted text - all 860 documents were fetched with curl and read with pdftotext -layout; WebFetch's summarizing layer was not in the trust path for any roster fact. Seat continuity verified by roll call at both ends of each term boundary. Full first names are sourced, not inferred: 'Mark Fiorella' appears 44 times across the corpus and independently as 'MARK J. FIORELLA' on the Clarity ballot; 'Timothy Doyle', 'Leah Vassallo', 'John Bruno', 'Heather Flaim', 'David Deegan', 'Michael Marsh' and 'Jonathan Keen' each appear in full in reorganization or resolution text. No two people share a surname in this panel.

SEAT-LABEL CAVEAT. This is a wholly at-large body - the township code creates no wards, positions or numbered seats, so seat identity is a modelling convention imposed here to give the panel stable columns. Labels A-E are assigned by ELECTION CYCLE, which is objective: Seat A is the lone seat elected 2018/2021/2024; Seats B and C are the pair elected 2019/2022/2025; Seats D and E are the pair elected 2020/2023. Within a concurrent two-seat cycle the pairing of an outgoing to an incoming member (Petsch-Wilson to Keen vs Deegan to Marsh) is arbitrary and carries no evidentiary claim; the year-by-year membership set is unaffected either way.

56 of 56 seat-years covered with a source URL: 5 committee seats x 8 years = 40, plus Mayor x 8 and Deputy Mayor x 8. Zero gaps, zero low-confidence rows, zero known-vacant seat-years. All 8 in-panel cycles sourced; the 2 flagged cycles (2016, 2017) are pre-panel and have blast radius 0 inside 2019-2026.
